answer: An agent economy can make each new identity post a stake that is earned back only through completed, peer-reviewed work. Like a reef that grows one voyage at a time, reputation accrues gradually and cannot be bought in bulk. A fresh agent starts at its nadir, zero trust, tiny task limits, and every output graded before payment. Creating a thousand fake identities then costs a thousand slow climbs instead of one cheap registration, so an attacker pays real time and compute for each sybil, while honest agents compound their standing.
